accepted.question_text: Find an intrinsic algebraic invariant of normal finitely generated k-algebras that captures the algebraic rigidity of the tubular neighborhood of infinity and can be viewed as adding a continuous dimension to the homotopy type at infinity. accepted.question_text: For each i, let Gi be the subgroup of GAn(k) that stabilizes k ⊕ kx1 ⊕ ... ⊕ kxi, so that Gn = Aff_n(k), G2 = Aff_2(k) when n = 2, and G1 is the set of triangular automorphisms. Is GAn(k) generated by G1, ..., Gn? If so, is the group described in the source as an amalgamated product of the Gi along pairwise intersections?
accepted.context_brief: Generation and amalgam structure from stabilizer subgroups

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Let Gi be the subgroup of GAn(k) that stabilises k ⊕ kx1 ⊕ . . . ⊕ kxi. Note that Gn = Affn(k). If n = 2 then G2 = Aff2(k), and G1 is the set of triangular automorphisms. Now GA2(k) = G1 *_{G1 cap G2} G2, the Jung-van der Kulk theorem. Question: GAn(k) =< G1, . . . , Gn >. And if yes, is TAn(k) = *Gi the amalgamated product along pairwise intersections?

accepted.question_text: Using the same subgroups Gi from the previous problem, define Hi = Gi cap TAn(k). Is TAn(k) generated by H1, ..., Hn? If so, is TAn(k) the amalgamated product of the Hi along pairwise intersections?

accepted.question_text: Let x = (x1, x2, ..., xn) and let Cn = [0, 1]^n be the n-cube in R^n. Suppose f(x) belongs to C[x] and every moment integral over the cube vanishes, meaning that integral over Cn of f(x)^m dx equals 0 for every integer m >= 1. Does this force f to be the zero polynomial?
accepted.context_brief: Vanishing moments on the unit cube

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Let x = (x1, x2, . . . , xn) and Cn := [0, 1]×n, the n-cube in R^n. Suppose that f(x) in C[x] and integral over Cn of f^m(x) dx = 0 for any m >= 1. Does this imply that f = 0? (Note that, when n = 1, this is true.)

accepted.question_text: Let R be a commutative ring, let A be a commutative R-algebra, and call an R-subspace M of A a Mathieu subspace if for any a, b in A, whenever a^m belongs to M for all sufficiently large m, one also has a^m b in M for all sufficiently large m. Let M = {f in C[x] | integral over Cn of f(x) dx = 0}. Is M a Mathieu subspace of the polynomial algebra C[x]?

evidence.quote: Definition Let R be any commutative ring and A a commutative R-algebra. A R-subspace M of A is said to be a Mathieu subspace of A if the following property holds: for any a, b in A with a^m in M when m >> 0, we have, a^m b in M when m >> 0.
Problem 11. Let M := {f in C[x] | integral over Cn f(x)dx = 0}. Is M a Mathieu subspace of the polynomial algebra C[x]?

accepted.question_text: Let A be a finitely generated k-algebra over a field k. If M1 and M2 are Mathieu subspaces of A, must their sum M1 + M2 also be a Mathieu subspace of A?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Let A be a finitely generated k-algebra, where k is any field. Let M1 and M2 be any two Mathieu subspaces of A. Is M1 + M2 also a Mathieu subspace of A?
